products.name: Robinhood
products.key_insight: Robinhood is the most controversial case study in behavioral design because it reveals what happens when you apply consumer-app engagement techniques to financial instruments. The confetti animation on trades, the one-tap execution, the push notifications on price movements — these are standard mobile engagement patterns, except the 'engagement' involves real money and real financial risk. The SEC's 2021 investigation and subsequent $65M fine specifically cited Robinhood's gamification. Robinhood's defense — that simplicity democratizes access — is valid. The counterargument — that simplicity in high-stakes domains removes protective friction — is also valid. This tension makes Robinhood the defining case study for when behavioral design ethics actually matter.
